land.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, which 'declared independence on 3 March 1992' (infobox 'Independence from Yugoslavia: 3 March 1992')

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Yugoslav row runs to 1991; the republic's land passes in one piece.

capitals.name: Sarajevo
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Sarajevo'. Republika Srpska names Sarajevo as its de jure capital and governs from Banja Luka (Republika Srpska page); the infobox gives Sarajevo as the capital.

correction.text: Shape unchanged (13,439 km2, the land the Sarajevo government held); it holds for 1992-1993 only, because the Croat-held land of Herzeg-Bosnia joins the Federation from March 1994 (new keyframe bosnia-and-herzegovina_1994). The rest of the republic is Serb-held (Republika Srpska) and drawn as contested land from April 1992.

keyframe_review.note: 13,439 km2 is 26% of the infobox 51,209 km2 (Bosnia and Herzegovina page). The Dayton page says 'About 53% (13,955 km2) of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina was under Bosniak control', the same order of size, so I read the shape as the government-held land; the Bosnian War page says the Serbs 'seized control of approximately 70% of the country's territory' in 1992. No page gives a year-by-year front line, so the shape is not verified for 1992 and 1993 against any map.

correction.text: the government-held land plus the Croat-held Herzeg-Bosnia (Herzegovina around Mostar and the 'Herzeg-Bosnian Canton (Canton 10)', 'almost completely under control of Bosnian Croats (4,924 km2)'), which 'was to be joined with Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina' under the Washington Agreement of March 1994

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps one 13,439 km2 shape for 1992-1995. The three cantons are my reading of Herzeg-Bosnia's territory (the page gives 'about 30% of the country' in its proclaimed borders and no municipality list); the Serb-held remainder stays contested until Dayton. Area is about 24,000 km2, close to the Federation's 51% share at Dayton. The words 'Herzeg-Bosnian Canton (Canton 10)' and 'almost completely under control of Bosnian Croats (4,924 km2)' in the correction text are from the Dayton Agreement page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dayton_Agreement), not the Herzeg-Bosnia page.

50,953 km2 against the infobox 51,209 km2 (ratio 0.995): the whole republic after Dayton (signed in Paris 14 December 1995; Federation 51%, Republika Srpska 49%, Brcko District 'created in 2000 from land from both entities'). The Dayton event of December 1995 is drawn at this keyframe. The 'Croatia' in the shape's country list is a sliver of outline, not Croatian land.
51,071 km2 against 51,209 km2 (ratio 0.997); no territorial change from 1996, the 0.2% difference is outline detail. Brcko District (2000) sits inside the shape.
Same outline as 2006 (51,071 km2); the page records no frontier change to 2024.

region.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina, the whole republic

ledger.note: 1992-03: Bosnia and Herzegovina declares independence from Yugoslavia. 'Bosnia and Herzegovina declared independence on 3 March 1992', after the referendum of 29 February and 1 March; it 'received international recognition the following month on 6 April 1992' and was admitted to the United Nations on 22 May 1992. Cliopatria draws only the government-held part from 1992.

region.text: the land the Bosnian Serbs seized; at Dayton it became Republika Srpska (49% of the country)

ledger.note: 1992-04: the Bosnian War begins and the Serbs take most of the country. 'the war is commonly seen as having started on 6 April 1992' when 'Serb forces began shelling Sarajevo'; the Serbs 'seized control of approximately 70% of the country's territory' in 1992. The Bosnian Serbs had proclaimed their republic on 9 January 1992 (renamed Republika Srpska on 12 August 1992). The zone drawn is the 1995 Republika Srpska, so it understates the 1992 Serb-held share.

region.text: Herzegovina around Mostar and the Herzeg-Bosnian Canton, held by the Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia

ledger.note: 1992-10: the Croat-Bosniak War begins (Herzeg-Bosnia page infobox 'Croat–Bosniak War: 18 October 1992'); Croats and Bosniaks fight over Herzegovina and central Bosnia, and 'in early 1993 the Croat-Bosniak War escalated'; Herzeg-Bosnia was declared a republic on 28 August 1993. The Constitutional Court had declared Herzeg-Bosnia unconstitutional on 14 September 1992. [Review eu-22-e: re-dated from 1993 to the infobox start, since the contest starts with the first fighting over ground, not the escalation.]

region.text: Herzegovina around Mostar and the Herzeg-Bosnian Canton

ledger.note: 1994-03: the Washington Agreement ends the Croat-Bosniak war. 'In March 1994, the Washington Agreement was signed that ended the conflict between Croats and Bosniaks' (18 March on the page).

region.text: the Croat-held land that 'was to be joined with Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina'

ledger.note: 1994-03: Herzeg-Bosnia's land passes to the new Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The page says the entity was 'to be joined' to the Federation and that on 14 August 1996 it 'would be formally abolished by the end of that month'; I draw the land as the state's from March 1994.

region.text: Republika Srpska as drawn at Dayton

ledger.note: 1995-11: the Bosnian War ends. 'It ended on 21 November 1995 when the Dayton Accords were initialed'; cease-fires had been agreed on 14 September and 5 October 1995.

region.text: Republika Srpska, 'Their percentage grew to 49% (48% by excluding the Brcko District, 24,526 km2)'

ledger.note: 1995-12: the Dayton Agreement is signed in Paris and Republika Srpska becomes an entity of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 'the agreement was signed ceremonially in Paris on 14 December 1995'; 'The State of Bosnia Herzegovina is composed of the' Federation and Republika Srpska. The Republika Srpska page gives 'Recognised as part of Bosnia and Herzegovina: 14 December 1995'.

1995-12: after Dayton the official name becomes Bosnia and Herzegovina. The page says 'the official name was changed to Bosnia and Herzegovina' after the Dayton Agreement and gives no day; the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is the same state.

wars.name: Bosnian War
wars.outcome: Ended 21 November 1995 with the initialling of the Dayton Accords (signed in Paris on 14 December): the republic keeps its international borders and is divided into the Federation (51%) and Republika Srpska (49%); Herzeg-Bosnia is abolished in 1996.
wars.note: The page names these three parties in the passages read; other states' roles (Serbia, Croatia, the JNA) are not drawn from this page. Start 6 April 1992 and end 21 November 1995 are the infobox dates.

wars.name: Croat-Bosniak War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Washington Agreement of March 1994, which joined Herzeg-Bosnia with the Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
wars.note: The Herzeg-Bosnia page lists the war's start as 18 October 1992 and says it 'escalated' in early 1993; the page also says Herzeg-Bosnia 'formally recognized the Government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina' and that tensions rose 'throughout late 1992'.

certainty.note: The front lines of the Bosnian War are approximate and the pages give none year by year; the external frontier is the former republic boundary with Croatia and Serbia-Montenegro and was not changed.

The external frontier is the former Yugoslav republic boundary, and the Inter-Entity Boundary Line 'essentially follows the front lines at the end of the Bosnian War' (Republika Srpska page); Brcko District (2000) is an arbitrated internal condominium.

notes: Cliopatria's 1992-1995 shape (13,439 km2) is read as the government-held land, not the recognised territory (51,209 km2); the Serb-held and Croat-held remainder is expressed as contest zones against republika-srpska and croatian-republic-of-herzeg-bosnia, which need dossiers (type rebel or state; eu-22-x scope: 'the Yugoslav war fronts and the Dayton entities'). Not settled with the pages opened: the yearly front lines 1992-1995 (the Serb share is about 70% in 1992 on the Bosnian War page and 49% at Dayton on the Dayton page; the page budget did not allow the 1995 offensives), the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia (Abdic, 1993-1995; the Bosnian War page does not mention it), Croatian and Yugoslav involvement, and the Brcko arbitration (the Bosnia page says only that the district 'was created in 2000 from land from both entities'). The Natural Earth admin-1 names for the entities are misspelled in the gazetteer ('Repuplika Srpska'); the dossier uses them as the gazetteer spells them. Herzeg-Bosnia's zone is three cantons, an approximation: central Bosnian Croat enclaves and Posavina are not included.
